questions.solution: The blocking electrons are internal : 2 + 8 = 10. Z_eff ≈ 11 − 10 = 1.

commonErrors.why: You wrote the entire nuclear charge. The outer electron does not feel all of it Because the internal electrons block part of it.
You wrote the number of blocking electrons. It is the subtract, not the result.
You added instead of subtracting. Blocking reduces net attraction, not increases it.

questions.solution: Distribution 2, 8, 6 There are three occupied levels, and the element is in the third cycle.

commonErrors.why: You wrote the atomic number. The period number is the highest occupied level, not the number of electrons.
You wrote the number of valence electrons. This defines the group, not the course.
You only counted completely filled levels. The third level is occupied, even if it is not full, it is counted.

questions.solution: The distribution is 2, 8, 3, so there are three electrons in the last level.

commonErrors.why: You wrote the entire atomic number. Valence electrons are the electrons of the last level alone.
You wrote inner electrons. It is the obscured, not the equal.
You wrote the capacity of the level, not what was actually occupied with it.

questions.solution: Z_eff(Cl) = 17 − 10 = 7 and Z_eff(Na) = 11 − 10 = 1, 6. difference This is why the chlorine atom is smaller and its ionization energy is greater, even though it has more electrons.

commonErrors.why: You added the two atomic numbers. What is required is the difference between two effective charges, not their sum.
You wrote Z_eff for chlorine alone. The amount of increase required, i.e. the difference between the two values.
You subtracted the blocking electrons twice, or calculated 17 − 11 + 10.

questions.solution: Blocking from internal levels alone: 2 + 8 = 10. The five in the last level are valence electrons, and we neglect to block them in this approximation.

commonErrors.why: You counted all the electrons. The electron does not obscure itself, The last level electrons are not blocking in this approximation.
You counted the valence electrons. She is the veiled one, not the veiled one.
You counted the first level alone. Blocking includes all internal levels.

questions.solution: The three orbitals are occupied singly before the pairing.

commonErrors.why: Electrons are paired before occupying equal-energy orbitals individually.
